tagline: Your Raspberry Pi 5, one confident step at a time.
one_liner: A premium, finishable learning platform that turns the 447-page Raspberry Pi 5 Handbook into a guided light/dark course where every terminal command and GPIO circuit becomes something a nervous beginner can actually run, safely, in the browser.
chosen_direction:
BASE = Concept A "Pi Pathway" (the Friendly Modern Course). It is the only one of the three that is unambiguously a usable beginner course first and a portfolio piece second: a finishable winding learning path, comfortable reading measure, warm encouraging gamification, and the clearest "this is a product, not a PDF" signal. A 55-year-old beginner exhales; that is the job. I am keeping A's information architecture (Path home → focused Reader → Tools), its motion philosophy (gentle spring, fully reversible, reduced-motion first-class), its gamification tuned-for-adults (no punishing streaks, micro-checks not exams, doing-is-the-quiz), and its product name finalist "Pilot" (chosen over "Pi Pathway" because it is one warm word, puns on pi/pilot/guiding, and sits alongside the creator's other one-word product names THE CONSTRUCT / RED MATRIX). 

GRAFTED FROM B "Workbench OS": (1) the actual TERMINAL ENGINE design — a real REPL with up-arrow history, tab-completion, persistent scrollback, and content-aware commands (`man <term>` pulls the glossary, `find <word>` full-text searches all 24 sections, `ls` lists chapters) — so the terminal doubles as the site's search and is genuinely functional, not a styled box. (2) The DARK MODE is promoted from an afterthought to a co-equal, fully-realised "Workbench" theme (graphite + raspberry + a single breathing green power-LED + optional 4%-opacity scanlines) so the app can deliver the cyberpunk/hardware wow the creator's portfolio leans on — the user toggles between "Daylight" (A's airy warm course) and "Workbench" (B's maker's-bench-at-night). (3) The breadboard's REAL electrical rules (series resistor required, LED polarity, no shorts, continuous power rails, a–e/f–j split) and the friendly validator hints. (4) The skippable boot micro-animation, demoted to a 1.2s optional flourish only in Workbench theme, never blocking content.

GRAFTED FROM C "Field Guide": (1) the HERO BOARD INSPECTOR — the same labelled Pi 5 board SVG already in ch01/ch02, made click-to-explore (tap USB-C, GPIO header, PCIe/SSD, RAM, activity LED → plain-English tooltip → deep-link to the chapter that uses it). This is the recurring hero object and reuses content that already exists. (2) The PROJECT "POWER-ON" PREVIEW CARDS for Part IV (a mock Pi-hole dashboard ticking up blocked-ad counts, a streaming local-AI chat bubble) that sell the payoff before the work. (3) The trace-fill "current flowing through copper" completion animation on the path connectors (electricity literally reaching the next node), grafted onto A's path as the lesson-complete reward. (4) Export/import of progress as JSON and a printable completion certificate, so progress survives reinstalls — important for a localStorage-only PWA. 

CONFLICTS RESOLVED: (a) Light-vs-dark — resolved as a true dual-theme product with Daylight as the DEFAULT (friendliness wins the first impression; a beginner must not land on a "console that might bite"), Workbench one toggle away. Both themes are fully contrast-checked. (b) Spatial-map-vs-linear-path (C vs A) — the winding vertical PATH wins over C's pan/zoom PCB map, because pan/zoom is a usability tax on nervous beginners and mobile; C's spatial flavour survives as the copper trace-fill animation and the lit/dim node states, not as the primary navigation. (c) Terminal-as-primary-nav (B) vs reader-first (A) — reader-first wins; the terminal is a powerful tool and the ⌘K search backend, never the only way in. (d) Streaks — A's gentle optional streak is kept but explicitly dismissible and never the spine; the Progress Core ring (from C) is the spine.

typography.scale_note: Fluid clamp() type, mobile-first. Body 17px base (1.65 line-height, max ~68ch measure in the Reader). Fraunces is THE signature detail: its optical-size (opsz) axis is tied to render size — hero/chapter titles render large = soft and curvy and human (the Brilliant/Duolingo warmth), inline/small Fraunces renders sturdier; this single typographic move is what keeps the app from reading like a tech manual. Inter for all running text, UI, callouts, tables. JetBrains Mono with ligatures OFF (beginner clarity) for every dark terminal block, inline code chips, GPIO pin labels, and the live sandboxes. All three self-hosted as woff2 for offline/PWA + zero layout shift, with a system fallback stack (ui-serif / system-ui / ui-monospace). Mono used at 0.16em letter-spacing for UPPERCASE eyebrow/kicker labels only.

motion: Philosophy: "gentle, physical, rewarding" — short spring-eased transitions (cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), 220–420ms), never flashy, always reversible-feeling. prefers-reduced-motion is FIRST-CLASS: every spring collapses to a single 120ms fade, the path trace-fill snaps to its end state, the power-LED goes static, scanlines off, parallax frozen — progress is never lost, only the flourish. Five signature moments: (1) LESSON-COMPLETE BLOOM + TRACE-FILL — finishing a lesson snaps the chapter's circular progress ring closed with a spring, puffs a short raspberry confetti-of-dots (canvas, ~600ms, then GC'd), AND sends a copper/raspberry pulse travelling along the SVG path connector to the next node (stroke-dashoffset tween, grafted from Concept C) which then 'powers on' by lifting 4px — progress is literally electricity reaching new territory. (2) PATH-DRAW REVEAL — the dotted circuit-trace connectors between path nodes draw themselves via stroke-dashoffset as they scroll into view (IntersectionObserver), like a PCB trace being etched, so the journey appears ahead of you. (3) COPY-COMMAND SATISFACTION — hovering a terminal block lifts it 2px and reveals Copy; clicking sweeps a thin raspberry highlight left-to-right across the line, morphs the button to a teal check with a 1px scale-bounce. (4) THEME SWEEP — the Daylight↔Workbench toggle is a sunrise/sunset wipe across the whole viewport, not an instant flip. (5) BOARD WAKE — the hero Pi 5 board's GPIO pins ripple-illuminate left-to-right on load and the activity LED does a two-blink 'boot' then settles to a slow breathing pulse (static in reduced-motion / Daylight-calm). The in-Workbench-only boot POST log is a 1.2s skippable, once-per-session flourish that never blocks content.

hero.concept: A calm, airy hero on warm off-white (Daylight default). LEFT: an oversized Fraunces headline with a soft raspberry accent on 'Raspberry Pi 5', a one-line subhead in the book's warm voice, and two buttons (solid raspberry primary, ghost secondary). A reassurance strip beneath: 'No experience needed · Works offline · Free · Nothing here can break your Pi'. RIGHT: the click-to-explore HERO BOARD INSPECTOR — the exact labelled Pi 5 board SVG already in ch01/ch02, restyled, where the 40-pin header slow-breathes, one green LED on a tiny breadboard softly pulses (a live preview of the GPIO sim), and tapping any real component (USB-C, GPIO header, PCIe/SSD, RAM, activity LED) pops a plain-English tooltip that deep-links to the chapter using it. Scroll one notch and the hero cross-fades into the START of the learning path (Part I node glowing 'Begin here') so the first scroll already steps onto the journey. In Workbench theme the same hero reframes as a dark bench-at-night with a breathing power-LED in the top bar.
hero.headline: Learn your Raspberry Pi 5. From first boot to building real things.
hero.sub: The complete 447-page handbook, reborn as a friendly course you can actually finish — with a real Pi terminal and a wireable circuit board you can try right here in your browser.

information_architecture: Single-page app, vanilla-JS ES-module hash router (#/path, #/chapter/ch12, #/glossary, #/reference, #/me) so it works on GitHub Pages, deep-links, and offline. THREE primary surfaces. (1) THE PATH (home, #/path): a vertical winding Duolingo-style trail of 24 lesson nodes grouped into the book's 6 Parts (Getting Started · Learning the System · Making Things · Projects · Looking After It · Reference) — node order and grouping taken verbatim from content/manifest.json's parts[]. Each node is a soft card with an icon, the manifest's read_min estimate, and a circular progress ring; dotted circuit-trace connectors draw between them on scroll. Part IV renders as bigger 'milestone' project cards (Media Centre, Retro Gaming, Pi-hole, Home Server, Home Assistant, Docker, Ollama AI). A glowing 'you are here' berry marker sits at the last-visited node. Sticky slim top bar = Progress Core ring + Daylight/Workbench toggle + ⌘K search. (2) THE READER (#/chapter/<id>): fetches the existing content/chapters/<id>.html fragment and renders it with restyled course components mapped 1:1 to the real class vocabulary already in the files — .lead, .explain ('what this does'), .code (dark terminal block), .jargon & .note & .tip & .warn (callouts), .steps, .tbl, .fig (SVG diagrams), .keyterms, .summary. ~68ch measure; left rail = per-chapter section outline (h2 ids already injected by transform.py) with scroll-spy; top reading-progress trace; sticky prev/next from manifest.order; and the data-widget mount divs (already present: terminal in ch06, gpio+resistor in ch12, picker in ch13) hydrate into the live sandboxes. (3) TOOLS: Glossary (searchable A–Z from content/glossary.json, 90 terms), Quick-Reference (apxA rebuilt as a filterable copyable command card), and 'My Pi' dashboard (#/me). Content is fetched per-chapter and service-worker cached for offline; the path/progress shell loads instantly. MOBILE-FIRST: path becomes a single-column swipeable trail; Reader's outline collapses to a bottom 'jump to' sheet; terminal/GPIO sandboxes go full-width with large touch targets; top bar shrinks to Progress Core + hamburger.
progress_and_gamification: Friendly and encouraging, never anxious — Brilliant/Duolingo tuned for a nervous adult, all client-side localStorage so it works offline in the installed PWA. (1) PROGRESS CORE: the ever-present ring in the top bar (e.g. '63% · 15/24') is the spine and doubles as the home button. Each chapter has its own completion ring that fills as you scroll its sections and snaps closed with the bloom animation at the summary or on 'Mark complete'. (2) NODE STATES on the path: not-started (dim) → in-progress (outlined) → done (lit + raspberry glow + copper trace pulsing to the next node); Part IV project nodes get a distinct 'built' trophy state. (3) MICRO-CHECKS, NOT EXAMS: end-of-chapter, 2–4 light tap-a-card check-ins drawn from each chapter's .keyterms/.summary, warm feedback, ZERO penalty for wrong answers, peek-the-answer always allowed (quizzes live in content/quizzes/, currently empty → authored during build). Crucially, the Terminal sandbox's guided mode and the GPIO 'it blinks!' moment ARE the assessment for those chapters — you prove understanding by doing. (4) BADGES mapped exactly to the book's real milestones: First Boot (ch04), Terminal Tamer (ch06), It Blinks! (ch12), Ad-Blocker Up (ch15), Home Server Online (ch16), AI on the Pi (ch19) — rendered as little SVG electronic components (LED, resistor, chip) filling a 'parts tray' on the My Pi dashboard. (5) A single gentle, dismissible 'continue where you left off' nudge on return; an OPTIONAL daily streak that is never the spine and never nags. (6) EXPORT/IMPORT progress as JSON + a printable completion certificate at 100% (grafted from Concept C) so progress survives reinstalls.

signature_features.name: The Learning Path
signature_features.what: The home screen: a vertical winding trail of all 24 lesson nodes grouped into the 6 Parts, with persisted not-started/in-progress/done state, circular progress rings, a 'you are here' berry marker, and dotted circuit-trace connectors that draw on scroll and pulse copper when you complete a node. Part IV projects are bigger milestone cards so the payoff is visible from day one.
signature_features.where: Home (#/path); the spine of the whole app
signature_features.build_notes: Drive entirely from content/manifest.json parts[]/order[]/read_min. Node state + Progress Core in localStorage. Connectors are one SVG per segment animated with stroke-dashoffset via IntersectionObserver. This is the single clearest 'product not PDF' signal and the main reviewer screenshot.

signature_features.name: Pi Terminal Sandbox
signature_features.what: A fully simulated Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm shell with a hand-written command parser and a tiny virtual filesystem (home/pi with the book's example folders). Implements the exact commands the book teaches — pwd, ls, ls -l, cd, mkdir, touch, cat, less, clear, whoami, uname -a — plus believable canned logs for sudo apt update / apt install (does nothing real). Up-arrow history, tab-completion, persistent scrollback. Content-aware super-powers grafted from Concept B: `man <term>` pulls the plain-English definition straight from glossary.json, `find <word>` full-text searches all 24 sections via search-index.json and prints clickable results, `ls` can list chapters — so the terminal IS the search backend behind ⌘K. Guided mode highlights the next command the chapter expects and gives a green check; unknown commands get a kind on-brand hint, never a scary error. One on-theme easter egg (sudo make-coffee).
signature_features.where: Hydrates the data-widget="terminal" mount already present in ch06; also reachable as a Tool and as the ⌘K search engine
signature_features.build_notes: This is the headline 'how is this a static site?' feature. Mirrors the in-browser engines in THE CONSTRUCT. search-index.json is ~775KB → lazy-load it only when the terminal/⌘K first opens; cache via service worker.

signature_features.name: GPIO & Breadboard Playground
signature_features.what: An interactive version of the labelled 40-pin SVG already in ch12 (reuse its exact color legend: orange 3.3V / red 5V / grey GND / purple GPIO / teal special) beside a virtual breadboard. The learner drags a jumper wire + 330Ω resistor + LED onto the correct pins (the book stars GPIO 17 for the LED and GPIO 27 for the button — use those exact pins), then presses Run on the book's actual gpiozero snippet (LED(17).blink()) and the on-screen LED blinks in time. A virtual Button(27) demo lets them press it and watch the LED respond. Real electrical rules enforced (series resistor required, LED polarity, no shorts, continuous power rails, a–e/f–j centre-gap split — grafted from Concept B's breadboard) with forgiving hints ('the LED looks backwards — try flipping it'). A baked-in 3.3V SAFETY GUARD: wiring 5V to a signal pin flares the wire red with the book's EXACT warning copy ('The GPIO pins operate at 3.3V logic. If you connect anything that pushes 5V into a GPIO input pin, you will permanently damage the Pi 5') — turning the book's scariest paragraph into a safe, memorable lesson. Hover-to-identify pinout overlay (physical vs BCM) doubles as a quick-reference.
signature_features.where: Hydrates data-widget="gpio" (and ="resistor" for the resistor/Ohm helper) mounts already present in ch12; pinout overlay also linked from apxA section 12
signature_features.build_notes: The centerpiece maker moment and the clearest SVG/state/animation craft. The warning text and starred pins are real handbook content — quote them verbatim for authenticity.

signature_features.name: Hero Board Inspector
signature_features.what: The labelled Raspberry Pi 5 board SVG (already in ch01/ch02) rebuilt as a click-to-explore object: hover/tap any real component — USB-C power, 40-pin GPIO header, micro-HDMI, PCIe/SSD connector, RAM, activity LED — pops a plain-English tooltip ('this is where power comes in') and deep-links to the chapter that uses it; a 'flip board' toggle shows the underside. It is the recurring hero object on the landing page and inside 'Meet the Pi' / 'Your Kit Unboxed'.
signature_features.where: Landing hero (right side) + embedded in ch01 and ch02
signature_features.build_notes: Grafted from Concept C. Reuses an SVG that already exists in two chapters — high wow, low new-asset cost. Component→chapter links use manifest ids.

signature_features.name: Command Palette + Living Glossary & Quick-Reference
signature_features.what: A ⌘/Ctrl-K palette searches all 24 chapters, the 90-term glossary, and the apxA command quick-reference at once with fuzzy matching and keyboard nav (backed by the same search-index.json + glossary.json the terminal uses). Every glossary term in running prose gets a dotted underline that pops a hover/tap 'definition card' without leaving the page — so a beginner never hits an unexplained word. The Quick-Reference chapter (apxA) becomes a filterable, one-click-copyable command cheat-sheet (search 'network' → every relevant command with its 'what this does' explainer).
signature_features.where: Global top bar (⌘K) everywhere; inline term-linking in the Reader; apxA and glos as Tools
signature_features.build_notes: Auto-link glossary terms by scanning rendered .explain/prose text against glossary.json keys at hydrate time (longest-match, skip inside .code blocks). Recently-viewed/bookmarked terms persist.

signature_features.name: My Pi Dashboard, Badges & Project Power-On Previews
signature_features.what: A localStorage progress hub: per-chapter completion, the overall Progress Core ring, the parts-tray of earned SVG-component badges, a gentle 'what to try next' nudge, and export/import + printable certificate. Each Part IV project also gets an animated 'what you're building' POWER-ON preview card (a mock Pi-hole dashboard with blocked-ad counts ticking up, a streaming local-AI chat bubble, a mock media library) plus a difficulty/time/what-you'll-need meter — selling the payoff before the work.
signature_features.where: My Pi (#/me) for the dashboard; the power-on preview cards live at the top of each Part IV project chapter (ch13–ch19) in the Reader
signature_features.build_notes: Power-on previews grafted from Concept C; pure CSS/JS mockups, no backend. Everything offline, optional, dismissible, never nagging.

signature_features.name: Workbench Theme + Installable Offline PWA
signature_features.what: A true second theme (one toggle from Daylight): graphite + raspberry, a single breathing green power-LED in the top bar, optional 4%-opacity CRT scanlines, and a 1.2s skippable once-per-session boot POST log — delivering the dark hardware wow the creator's portfolio leans on, without compromising the friendly default. The whole app is an installable offline-first PWA: a service worker pre-caches all 24 chapter fragments + manifest/glossary so it works on a train; a maskable raspberry+terminal-cursor icon; an Install chip.
signature_features.where: Global (theme toggle in top bar); service worker + manifest.webmanifest at app root
signature_features.build_notes: Grafted from Concept B. Both themes contrast-checked. Scanlines/boot/LED-pulse all respect prefers-reduced-motion. Theme choice persists in localStorage; default is Daylight.

component_style_notes: Map every restyled component to the EXACT class vocabulary already in content/chapters/*.html (counted in the source): .code (348 occurrences) = dark terminal block on code_bg #15131F with JetBrains Mono code_ink, a faux 'pi@raspberrypi:~ $' prompt header strip, optional line numbers, a Copy button (raspberry sweep + teal-check feedback) and, where a data-widget terminal exists, a 'Try it' button that opens the sandbox pre-loaded with that command. .explain (348) = the 'what this does' block: a soft surface2 card with a teal (accent2) left-border and a small mono 'WHAT THIS DOES' eyebrow. .jargon (174) = inline plain-words definition, subtle warm-tinted inline card. .tip (128) = success-green left-accent card. .note (128) = neutral surface2 card with a thin line border. .warn (80) = danger-red left-accent card with a triangle glyph; the GPIO 3.3V warning gets extra prominence and is the copy the sim quotes. .steps (96) = numbered list with raspberry step badges, generous spacing. .tbl (100) = clean zebra-free table, mono in cells that hold commands, horizontal scroll on mobile, per-row copy where a cell is a command. .fig (47) = SVG figures in a captioned surface card; the ch12 pinout and ch01/ch02 board figures are upgraded in place to the interactive widgets. .keyterms (24) = chip row of glossary-linked terms at chapter end (feeds the micro-check). .summary (24) = a warm Fraunces-titled recap card that triggers the completion-ring snap. .lead (24) = larger Fraunces-tinted intro paragraph. CARDS generally = surface #FFFFFF on bg #FBF8F4, 1px line #E7DFD6 border, 16px radius, soft low shadow that lifts on hover. CALLOUTS share a left-accent-bar system color-coded by intent (teal=explain, green=tip, red=warn, neutral=note). QUIZZES (micro-checks) = tap-card multiple choice, raspberry selected state, green/encouraging feedback, no red 'wrong' shaming, peek-answer link. SIDEBAR (Reader left rail) = quiet mono section list with a scroll-spy active indicator (raspberry tick) and a thin progress trace at the very top. All components must re-skin cleanly under both Daylight and Workbench via CSS custom properties only — no per-theme markup.
differentiators: A real, hand-written Raspberry Pi OS terminal REPL in vanilla JS — virtual filesystem, history, tab-completion — that also powers the site's search (man/find/ls), so the navigation IS the skill the book teaches

A working GPIO + breadboard simulator built from the book's own starred pins (GPIO 17 LED, GPIO 27 button) and real gpiozero code, with enforced electrical rules and a 3.3V safety guard that quotes the handbook's exact damage warning — physical computing made safe before you buy a single LED

Dual co-equal themes: a warm Fraunces 'Daylight' course that makes a nervous beginner exhale, and a graphite 'Workbench' mode with a breathing power-LED that delivers the creator's signature dark-hardware portfolio wow — one sunrise/sunset toggle apart

A genuinely finishable 24-node learning PATH with copper trace-fill progress, reframing a 447-page PDF as a journey — not a spatial pan/zoom map that taxes beginners, but a single-column trail that works thumb-first on mobile

Built entirely from content that already exists: reuses the manifest, the per-chapter HTML fragments and their exact component classes, the labelled board + pinout SVGs, the 90-term glossary and the search index — zero-build, GitHub-Pages-deployable, installable offline PWA

Adult-grade gamification: doing-is-the-quiz, no punishing streaks, badges mapped to real Pi milestones (First Boot, It Blinks!, AI on the Pi), and exportable progress + a printable certificate so it survives reinstalls

An inline 'never get lost' safety net — every glossary term auto-links to a hover definition card, and ⌘K searches chapters + glossary + command reference at once — that makes 447 pages feel navigable, the polish that reads as Linear/Brilliant rather than a static site
must_avoid: Do NOT make the dark 'Workbench' theme the default or the first impression — a nervous adult beginner must land on the warm, airy Daylight course; dark is one deliberate toggle away

Do NOT use a pan/zoom spatial PCB map as primary navigation (Concept C's lobby) — it taxes beginners and is poor on mobile; the spatial flavour survives only as the trace-fill animation and node lit/dim states on the linear path
Do NOT let the terminal or 'type to navigate' be the only or primary way in (Concept B) — reader-first; the terminal is a powerful tool and the ⌘K backend, never a gate

Do NOT let the boot sequence, scanlines, or power-LED block, delay, or obscure content — boot is a 1.2s skippable once-per-session flourish, Workbench-only, and all ambience must vanish under prefers-reduced-motion

Do NOT invent component classes — render strictly against the existing vocabulary (.code .explain .jargon .tip .note .warn .steps .tbl .fig .keyterms .summary .lead .widget-mount) so the existing fragments and transform.py pipeline keep working
Do NOT use red as a 'wrong answer' shaming color in the micro-checks, and never penalise or block on a wrong answer — wrong is free, peek-the-answer is always offered
Do NOT eagerly load the ~775KB search-index.json on first paint — lazy-load it on first ⌘K / terminal open and cache it; the path shell must load instantly
Do NOT soften or paraphrase the GPIO 3.3V damage warning — quote the handbook copy verbatim in the safety guard; authenticity is the teaching point
Do NOT add any backend, framework, or build step — vanilla JS ES modules only, must deploy as static files on GitHub Pages and run fully offline
wordmark: Set in Fraunces at its soft optical-display setting, all-lowercase 'pilot', with the dot of the 'i' replaced by a small raspberry-red filled circle (a nod to both the Pi power-LED and the berry motif). The same red dot is the favicon / maskable PWA icon and the 'you are here' marker on the learning path. In Workbench theme the dot gains a faint green power-LED glow.
